content:
sanjay: quick dump — i profiled the long-seq KV-cache regression with nsys and perfetto. reproducer: synthetic seq ramp 32 -> 2048, batch 8, kv page=4MB. saw repeating DMA bursts that line up with KV span boundaries.

marie: nice, can you paste the nsys command you used?

sanjay: ran: `nsys profile --trace=cuda,cudnn,cuda_driver -o /tmp/trace.kv --sample=cpu --capture-range=cudaLaunch --force-overwrite --duration=180 python repro_longseq.py`

alex: perfetto capture? link?

sanjay: uploaded perfetto url: https://perfetto.community/trace/abc123 (private). look at GPU timeline + DMA transfers. the pattern: ~3.1us DMA latency spikes every ~8k tokens, BW ramp to ~420 GB/s HBM then back down.

tara: 420 GB/s seems suspiciously high for sustained bursts. is that copy throughput (device-host) or intra-device peer DMA?

sanjay: intra-device HBM DMA (nvlink-like path inside card). nvprof counters show copy engines active, plus kernel stalls on L2 miss. Kernel timeline shows tiny tensor ops blocking while DMA drains.

perf-sre: what about KV layout? are spans aligned to 2MB/4MB pages? misalignment can cause extra scatter-gather descriptors and DMA inefficiencies.

sanjay: exactly — spans are currently split by logical KV-window, not by physical page. when the span crosses 2MB boundary, we see ~15% higher descriptors and an extra 1.2us scatter overhead.

marie: can we test pinning pages / prefetching? maybe pre-reserve contiguous pages for hot KV spans?

sanjay: tried a quick experiment: prepin hot spans (mmap + mlock) before request burst. result: peak BW reduced variability, avg latency improved ~6% and fewer kernel stalls in timeline.

alex: interesting. what about changing eviction granularity? if we split large spans into smaller fixed-size slabs, does that increase descriptor count but reduce cross-page splits?

sanjay: i tested 4MB->1MB slab sizes. tradeoff: descriptor count up ~10% overall, but DMA bursts are smoother and kernel stall tail latency drops by ~18%. microbench attached in trace.

tara: did you check CUDA graph warmup? small microbatches + graph capture/launch can change timing of DMA vs kernel.

sanjay: good call — capture had graph capture on. reran without graph => DMA scheduling slightly different, but underlying misalignment still caused the big spikes. graph just amplified jitter when capture happens in critical path.

perf-sre: sounds like several mitigation paths: 1) align KV spans to large-page boundaries at allocation time; 2) prepin/prefetch hot spans; 3) adjust slab size to 1MB for longseq flows; 4) prefer async copy streams + overlap policy changes so kernels yield while DMA drains.

marie: could we change kernel selection heuristic to prefer kernels that tolerate intermittent BW drops (higher compute-bound kernels) when longseq detected? maybe choose fused attention variant with higher compute intensity.

alex: yes, runtime could switch kernel variant based on observed HBM occupancy. need a cheap estimator: sample HBM utilization every N requests, trigger kernel variant if sustained BW jitter > threshold.

sanjay: i prototyped a sampling hook: every 500 requests sample perf counter `dram_util` and if > 70% variance we switch to `compute-heavy-attn-v2`. latency tradeoff ~+4% median but tail -20%.

tara: sounds promising. please push the nsys perf artifacts + small repro script to /tmp/artifacts and open a PR with the sampling hook.

sanjay: will do. uploading artifacts now and making a small branch. cc @dev-bot for CI perf-run.

dev-bot: perf CI job queued: run/longseq-kv-bandwidth-probe (id: 2026-11-04-07).

perf-sre: next steps: 1) confirm page-alignment allocator for KV, 2) run larger scale job on dedicated instance to ensure no NUMA cross-talk, 3) add automatic kernel-variant fallback in runtime. i'll create tickets.

marie: thanks — this explains a lot of the tail spikes we've seen in customer traces. small follow-up: can you include a short annotated perfetto screenshot in the ticket showing the DMA bursts aligned to KV-span boundaries? that will help infra folks.

sanjay: yup will attach screenshot + nsys timeline + summary numbers (peak BW 420 GB/s, dma-latency 3.1us spikes, tail-latency reduction 18% with 1MB slabs).

alex: awesome. ping when PR is up and i'll try the slab rollout on a dedicated pool. :thumbsup:
